steps.name: Maria
steps.text: *yawn*... Is it morning already?

steps.name: Maria
steps.text: The operators' equipment was a lot more seriously damaged than we anticipated... Still, the fact that they managed to save so many people from that Catastrophe is a testament to how amazing they are.

steps.name: Maria
steps.text: Mhm. I've got to chin up as well.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Hi Maria, I'm here to pick up an order from the Engineering Department.

steps.name: Maria
steps.text: Oh, Grani! Just a moment. Let's see... where did I put that? Sorry, I haven't tidied this place up for a few days, so it's a bit of a dump.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Ahaha... It sure looks more like a proper Kazimierzian workshop than the last time I stopped by. Huh? What's this?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: A novel?

steps.name: Maria
steps.text: 'The Last Knight'! What's that doing here? Did it get stuck underneath the blueprints when I was flipping through my boxes and drawers yesterday? I was wondering where it had gone.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: 'The Last Knight'?

steps.name: Maria
steps.text: It used to be my favorite book. My sister gave it to me as a gift when I was little.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: A knight novel from Kazimierz, huh?

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Mind lending it to me?

steps.name: Maria
steps.text: Sure thing!

steps.name: Maria
steps.text: Ugh, so that's where the book on Arts Unit theory ended up... Sorry Grani, this might take a while. I can bring it over to you later, if you like.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: Don't worry, it's not urgent. Just means I get to stay on Rhodes Island a bit longer this time.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: I'll just be over here reading, to pass the time.

steps.name: Maria
steps.text: I'm really, really sorry about this.
'The Last Knight.'
The title is as pompous as it is cliché. There have probably been hundreds of books written about the last knight, the swiftest knight, or the strongest knight.
But seeing how the Radiant Knight gifted it to her own sister, surely there must be more to it than that?
With that thought, Grani opens it up, only to find a bookmark wedged inside.
Written in wobbly Kazimierzian letters is a line that may well have been copied from the book.

steps.name: Grani
steps.text: 'If you deem the waves too raucous, then command the ocean to be still.' Huh...?
Legend has it that the Last Knight returned to Iberia. The enemies reflected in his eyes were not living creatures, but rather, he charged at the mountains, the cities, and the waves.
Legend has it that the Last Knight settled by the coast, sustaining himself on the wind and taking shelter in the mist, until at last he forgot how to remove his helmet.

Legend has it that the Last Knight finally disappeared after clashing against the great waves. His family discovered what he'd left behind along the shore and brought it back to the Land of Knights, burying it deep in the mountains.

Legend has it that his or her story was brought to light by a poet. Embellished, sung, given both meaning and symbolism. And in this form, they did finally return to the Land of Knights, as a highly controversial figure.
However...
...There are some who believe that the mad knight triumphed over the ocean, over time, over death itself. That his quest continues until the end of all things.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: What... are you?
The knight does not answer. His deathly gaze is fixed on Gladiia.
However, she quickly realizes that he is not actually looking at her.
He stares only at the key in her hands.
Guh... *cough* *cough*... Hiss...
The knight opens his mouth as if to speak. But only a shriveled rasp comes forth, like the sound of muscle tearing.
He begins to take a step forward.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Where did you get that key?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Oh, I did not intend to... pry into Rhodes Island's internal affairs.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: But that is Breogan's legacy, passed through the hands of the four Feranmuts to once again return to that Abyssal Hunter.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: By pure coincidence, one of the Hunters found it in Kazimierz.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: ...Kazimierz? What a distant land. I still remember journeying with my mentor to receive an envoy from the Land of Knights, and secretly overhearing a few Silverlance campaign knights describing their ideals.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: I hear the country has changed considerably since then.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: For better or worse, every political entity has undergone similar changes in our current era. But that has nothing to do with Iberia.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: We are like ensnared beasts. Should we struggle, we suffer and bleed. Should we give up, our lives are forfeit.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Before we unmask those still-human traitors, I have a new question for you, Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: No doubt you've already realized this, but that child couldn't possibly be Breogan's descendant. The Inquisition would not have missed such a vital clue.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: So why would you still condemn him to a meaningless death?

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Calls out to its kin with a slithering sound)

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: High Inquisitor!

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: ...Their numbers are increasing. But, none of them showed up until we reached the lighthouse.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: S-Sir, I've found a way to open the main door!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But the Eye of Iberia's core facilities are at the top of the tower. And it's very, very tall! The lift mechanism isn't working either, so we can only get up there by foot!

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Slithering sounds)

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: High Inquisitor, we need more time!

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Take the Ægir with you.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: There is no time to spare, Irene.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Aye! Right away!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Wait, hold on!

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Intense slithering sounds)

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Oh, are they here? No, the lantern's flames are flickering. Something has stepped into my Arts' domain.

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Cowering slithering sounds)

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: (They're scared. Strange, these things have never shown signs of fear before.)

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: (Confusion then? But what could be the cause...?)

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Confused slithering sounds)
The High Inquisitor raises his lantern high, and the Sea Terror in turn retreats into the shadows of the reef.
When he looks around once more, he notices the reef is littered with corroded and broken weapons, soaked with the fresh blood of monsters.
Arms belonging to the Inquisition. As his mentor Carmen had said, it is not as if the Inquisition had never considered reclaiming the sole remaining lighthouse.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Being unaffected by the Profound Silence, it's been quite well-preserved.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Even so, the Inquisition has never made a serious attempt to retrieve its own Eye following the Profound Silence.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: This place used to be a spectacular overlook. A breathtaking, unobstructed view of the entire city.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: It had been manned by Iberians, day in, day out.

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Cautious slithering sounds)

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: But you've taken it as a feeding ground, building a nest for your spawn without permission.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Hup...
Emotions.
Long-lost emotions.
From soldier to Inquisitor, and finally to one who sees the truth. He has been tempered, lost and reforged anew countless times. And thus, Dario became one of the few High Inquisitors in Iberia.
Only a single word separates an Inquisitor from a High Inquisitor, but that single word is the difference between heaven and earth.
He used to regard himself as resolute as steel. Before Iberia's enemies, his lantern would flicker, his sabre would glimmer, and every line of the Scriptures would be put into practice.
But now, he feels a type of strong emotion welling up within him. One not solely a product of the law and justice that is preached.

After acknowledging its rationality, High Inquisitor Dario accepts the fact that he is truly experiencing grief and anger. His handcannon takes aim at the Sea Terror, yet his eyes are directed towards the sea.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: When you die, mankind may thrive.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: These words are not a part of our laws or scriptures, but rather yours. 'Survival of the fittest.'

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Right here!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: It's just as the records say! The lighthouse relies on the power source located at its base, and the core column is divided into several areas. The console on this floor controls—

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...Controls what?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Uhh, signal recording.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: We should be able to put that to use later. But for now, we need to prioritize powering the entire lighthouse. Let's continue.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Hopefully all goes well until reinforcements arrive.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Ugh—!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: What's wrong, Doña Irene?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...It's nothing. Probably just my imagination. Maestro... the High Inquisitor is keeping guard outside. We'll be fine.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: A-Alright... After we restart the lighthouse's power system, we should be able to use the lift as well. That way the others will be able to catch up to us soon enough.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: So let's hurry!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: There's something odd about him. Some kind of... lingering scent.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: But what is it?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: The scent of another land. Nothing you'd be interested in.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: He is without a doubt a Seaborn. But not the same as Quintus.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: How is it possible for so many land creatures to become Seaborn though? They shouldn't have frequent contact with the ocean.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: With no way to communicate, we can do nothing but let his body lose all function.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: He's about to attack!
The knight suddenly seems to vanish in place. But for the senses of an Abyssal Hunter, catching him is hardly a challenge at all.
With his speed, he opts not to attack them, but instead leaps high into the air and bounds toward the lighthouse with a ferocious roar.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Graaaaaagh!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Woah... Wh-What was that?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Don't panic! Keep climbing!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Complete our mission: rekindle this lighthouse!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: R-Right!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: (These vibrations... Are the walls coming under attack? How is that possible? We're already dozens of meters above ground. Do the Sea Terrors have some sort of cannon?)

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: (Or... maybe some massive creature? But other than the tremor just now, I haven't noticed anything else.)

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: (Maestro...!)
The knight lifts his head and looks up. The lighthouse did not budge an inch.
He shakes his twisted weapon disapprovingly. This long spear, once the creation of a master craftsman, is now inundated with the scent of the depths.
He does not see the one standing in his way. The knight bends his knees again, intending to try once more.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: What are you doing?

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: You contemptuously provoke Iberia, trespass upon restricted areas, and damage a precious heritage site.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Just look at yourself. Do you have even a single shred of human-born dignity left in you?

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: ...Dig...nity...?

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Seems your vocal chords still work at least.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: (Unintelligible sounds) ...The sea... doesn't need.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Crush... the waves. Trample the sun. End the pain.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Things should not, remain the same. The great tree, takes root in this land.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Your stance. Your gray armor. And that spear.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: You're from Kazimierz?

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: I am... I am...

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Knight!

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: ...Slithering steel... Ocean's waves...

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: (Lifting the lantern won't do anything. There's no sign of any other ships coming.)

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: (The fluorescent nethersea brand ignored him. He may well be the source of the Sea Terrors' panic.)

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: (Then... is he actually a Seaborn disguised as a human?)

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: You seek to destroy the Eye of Iberia? The Inquisition will not allow it.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Aaaaaargh, the soil—!

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Now!

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: ...Good evening, Mister Knight.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Where are the other two?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: The others? They're... currently having a little chat with Mister Knight's friends.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: So a fight broke out not far away. Seems like it's a clash of civilizations then.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: It has nothing to do with me, though, so I came over here.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: You... You're different from how you were back in Sal Viento.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: And also from how you were when we met in Gran Faro. You're always changing.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: The seawater is sobering. Even the slightest breath of air brought in by the ocean breeze.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Although... I do want to return to the sea's embrace, but Skadi stopped me.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: My little Skadi. She's so scared... But of what?

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: With what's going on right now, I need Gladiia's explanation all the more.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: (Ægirian) Mister Knight, good sir, return to your sweet slumber, deep in the abyss.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: (Ægirian) We are not enemies.
The knight ignores Laurentina, who murmurs as if singing.
As for the 'enemy' who'd just dealt him a heavy blow, the knight only tilts his head slightly before quickly snapping his attention back to the towering lighthouse.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Alas, how tragic. Language can no longer reach your ears, just as those clouds cover your eyes.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Even in your madness, does your will still drive you forward like clockwork, compelling your body to advance?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Come then, storm.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Let us share this dance.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I've found it! The main control panel!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: How's it looking?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I, I'm not too sure. This is more complicated than what's on the diagrams, and, uh, I've never actually operated these things before.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: That sound again... What's going on outside?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Perhaps we're still underestimating the dangers we might encounter here. At this rate, holding out for the Penal Battalion's technicians might be...

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: No, even if reinforcements arrive, the sacrifices required to repair the lighthouse under these conditions are akin to setting up camp under the crosshairs of a high-speed warship.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Jordi, you're a civilian, and a part of Iberia. For now, I won't ask where you came from, or about what happened in Gran Faro's past.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: We're in a race against time. Right now, this instant, try your best to get all the information out of the Eye of Iberia as you can. Maestro and I will protect this tower, and we—

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: A-All right... I've managed to retrieve the logs. The panel is still responding, and the energy module underneath the tower is still functional.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...You act fast. Commendable.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: What's next? How long would it take to reboot the entire lighthouse?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I, I'll see what I can do!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Um... Even though I know the people out there are fighting against those sea monsters, I still have to say this!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: As long as the panel is still responding, it shouldn't be too hard to restart it. I've read about this in the notes my parents left behind... B-But, this would be my first time actually operating something like this, so it's still a bit of a gamble!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Either way, it all takes time! We should probably—

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Eek—!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Guard this place, right?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Don't look down. Keep moving forward.
